builtBy: nig/s77/quake_build/build_seismic_rule.py (v91.17.77 agent Q, from agent E s75 E2); inputs beside it
use: server/api/quake.mjs: the live earthquake overlay (GET /api/quake/live, /api/quake/replay). Events are an EVENT overlay: never added to the BCP-SP 2007 design-basis seismic zone (v89.44 FIX 5).
method: per event and tehsil: expected intensity (MMI) = the event's ShakeMap MMI grid where the event carries one (the highest grid value inside the tehsil; a tehsil with no grid cell inside takes the grid value at its nearest point to the epicentre), else the intensity prediction equation IPE(M, R_hypo) with R_hypo = sqrt(Re^2 + depth^2) and Re the great-circle km from the epicentre to the NEAREST point of the tehsil polygon (0 inside it). A tehsil is flagged at the highest level whose mmiMin the intensity reaches, only within the region buffer (bufferKm), and an equation value only inside the equation's validity (validity.mwMin-mwMax, distanceKmMax).

ipe.name: Allen, Wald & Worden (2012) hypocentral-distance intensity prediction equation, active crustal regions
ipe.sigmaNote: total sigma s1 + s2/(1+(R/s3)^2) in the source: about 0.8-1.2 MMI

validity.source: Allen et al. 2012 abstract: "moment magnitude MW 5.0-7.9 ... distances less than 300 km" https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10950-012-9278-7

ipe.outsideValidity: an event outside Mw 5.0-7.9 without a ShakeMap is shown on the map but flags no tehsil; a tehsil beyond 300 km is never flagged
ipe.citation: Allen, T.I., Wald, D.J., Worden, C.B. (2012) Intensity attenuation for active crustal regions. J. Seismology 16:409-433, doi:10.1007/s10950-012-9278-7
ipe.coeffSource: https://github.com/gem/oq-engine/blob/master/openquake/hazardlib/gsim/allen_2012_ipe.py (AllenEtAl2012Rhypo COEFFS), copy in quake_build/oq_allen_2012_ipe.py, read by build_seismic_rule.py

checkAgainstShakeMap.source: agent E ipe_vs_shakemap.json: ShakeMap MMI minus IPE over cells within 300 km, 11 Pakistan-region events (ShakeMap is itself GMPE/GMICE + DYFI, not ground truth)

levels.plain: very strong shaking or worse (moderate damage or worse possible)

levelSource: USGS ShakeMap intensity legend (perceived shaking / potential damage), https://earthquake.usgs.gov/product/shakemap/ci13936812/ci/1486496531537/download/tvguide.txt (copy: quake_build/tvguide.txt)
levelMapping: our levels <- ShakeMap intensity classes: Low = IV (Light shaking, no damage; E s75 "felt"), Moderate = V (Moderate shaking, Very Light damage; E "watch"), High = VI (Strong shaking, Light damage; E "act"), Severe = VII and above (Very Strong shaking, Moderate damage). A continuous MMI belongs to the class of its nearest integer, so class k starts at k - 0.5 [assumed rounding convention]. Normal = below IV (not felt or weak): not flagged.

alert.rule: a flagged tehsil at a level whose index (Normal 0 .. Severe 4) is at or above the client's alert threshold ALERT_MIN_CLASS_RANK joins the Alerts list and the "Check these" chip
alert.source: the client's one declared alert threshold (window.ALERT_MIN_CLASS_RANK = 3 = High in v91.17.76; AGN.hazards.alertThreshold); no second threshold is kept here
alert.windowBasis: [assumed] an earthquake stays in the Alerts list for 7 days after its origin time: the window of the 7-day feed customers saw in the seismic panel since v89 (the retired client loader); older events stay on the map overlay for retainDays. A replay (/api/quake/replay) is judged as if the event had just happened.

radiusKmTable.note: epicentral radius (km) where the IPE falls to each level's mmiMin inside the magnitude validity range; derived here for review only (the server evaluates the IPE)

region.bboxSource: agent E s75 counts.json query box (Pakistan tehsil union extent, rounded)
region.bufferBasis: min(IPE validity limit 300 km, IPE Low-level radius 989.3 km (MMI 3.5) of the 2005 Kashmir event (usp000e12e, Mw 7.6, 26 km): the largest onshore event of the instrumental record in the region). Events are kept when they fall inside the Pakistan box widened by bufferKm, so an event just across a border that can shake a tehsil is not missed.

poll.feedBasis: Cache-Control max-age of the two summary feeds, measured at build: 2.5_day 60 s, significant_week 60 s; the feeds are regenerated every minute (earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php)
poll.revisionBasis: [assumed] hourly; measured first-publication latency (E latency.json): M>=5 median 17.2 min, max 25.7 min; M<5 median 94.9 min, 58% after 60 min, max 14 days (late contributed events and magnitude or location revisions arrive through this query, not the feeds)

magMinBasis: catalogue completeness in the region: M>=2.5 and M>=4 returned 19 and 18 events over the same 30 days (E counts.json), so the M2.5 feed adds almost nothing below M4 here
retainBasis: [assumed] the 30-day window of E's counts; the map shows events, never adds them to the BCP design-basis zone (v89.44 FIX 5)

markerRadiusPx.basis: [assumed] display only: radius = base + perMagnitude x (M - magMin), so M4 is 4 px and M7 is 13 px

magnitudeCaveat: the IPE is fitted on moment magnitude; 2164 of 2295 M>=4 events in the region over 10 years carry mb (E counts.json), used as-is
depthCaveat: Hindu Kush intermediate-depth events (100-250 km) dominate the regional count (1437 of 2295 M>=4 deeper than 70 km over 10 years); the crustal IPE is applied with R_hypo, and the ShakeMap check above is the evidence it holds there

customerCredit.rule: customer screens name the feed only by the generic label; the supplier is named on the Sources tab (v76 hard rule)

licence.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
licence.note: same id as the data/open-feeds.json entry, so the Sources page shows one entry
